questions.skill: Use logarithms to find a term number
questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: a(n) = 3 · 4^(n-1). What is the smallest n for which a(n) > 10,000?
questions.prompt_markup:
a(n) = 3 · 4^(n-1).
What is the smallest n for which a(n) > 10,000?
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent form. 4^(n-1) > 3,333.3... gives n - 1 > log 3,333.3 ÷ log 4 ≈ 5.85. Check: a(6) = 3,072 and a(7) = 12,288.

questions.prompt: A sequence starts at 5 and grows by 20% per term: a(n) = 5(1.2)^(n-1). Which term is the first to exceed 100? (log means base 10.)
questions.prompt_markup: A sequence starts at 5 and grows by 20% per term: a(n) = 5(1.2)^(n-1). Which term is the first to exceed 100? (log means base 10.)
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent form. 1.2^(n-1) > 20 gives n - 1 > log 20 ÷ log 1.2 ≈ 16.4. Check: a(17) ≈ 92.4 and a(18) ≈ 110.9.
